Case 2

Zheng Mouli v. Ni Moubin — Divorce Dispute

--Judicial Determination of Threats as a Form of Domestic Violence

(1) Basic Facts

The plaintiff Zheng Mouli and the defendant Ni Moubin registered their marriage on February 11, 2009, and gave birth to a son, Ni Moumou, on May 7, 2010. During their cohabitation, the defendant regularly beat a basketball wrapped in a white cloth on which the words "I will beat Zheng Mouli to death" were written. On February 23, 2011, the plaintiff and defendant quarreled over family matters, and the defendant beat the plaintiff, causing minor injuries. On March 14, 2011, the plaintiff filed for divorce, requesting the court to grant the divorce; to award custody of the son to the plaintiff, with the plaintiff bearing the cost of child support; to divide the marital property; and to order the defendant to pay RMB 30,000 in compensation for mental distress.

(2) Judgment

The court found after trial that the plaintiff Zheng and the defendant Ni lacked understanding before marriage and married hastily. After marriage, the defendant hung a basketball wrapped in white cloth on the balcony of their home, with aggressive and threatening words written on the cloth, and frequently beat the basketball, tormenting the plaintiff visually and causing her fear. This behavior constituted emotional violence. When marital conflicts arose, the defendant inflicted physical violence on the plaintiff, causing minor injuries, ultimately leading to the complete breakdown of the marital relationship. Because the defendant had a history of domestic violence, he was not suitable to directly raise the child, and since the son was under two years old, living with the mother was more conducive to his physical and mental health. The defendant's domestic violence caused the plaintiff mental distress, and the defendant should bear fault liability. Therefore, the defendant was ordered to pay the plaintiff RMB 5,000 in compensation for mental distress. The judgment has taken effect.

Case 3

Chen Mouzhuan v. Zhang Mouqiang — Divorce Dispute

--Arbitrarily Imposed "Family Rules" Constituting Domestic Violence

(1) Basic Facts

The plaintiff Chen Mouzhuan and the defendant Zhang Mouqiang registered their marriage on August 16, 1988, and gave birth to a daughter, Zhang Moumou (now an adult), on July 9, 1989. Because she was frequently beaten and scolded by Zhang, Chen filed for divorce in 1989. Zhang admitted his mistake in court and promised not to be violent again, so Chen withdrew the lawsuit. After that, Zhang did not change and continued to demand that Chen obey him in everything. If she was not submissive enough, he would verbally abuse and threaten her, and sometimes beat her. On May 14, 2012, Zhang, claiming that Chen had not washed his clothes clean enough, scolded Chen and ordered her to rewash them. When Chen refused, Zhang beat her. Their daughter Zhang was also injured while trying to stop him. On May 17, 2012, Chen filed for divorce. The defendant Zhang argued in his reply that it was just a general marital dispute and promised not to beat Chen again. During the trial, Zhang was still rude, scolding Chen, and firmly opposed the divorce.

(2) Judgment

The court found after trial that domestic violence is a means for one spouse to control the other. The facts showed that Zhang imposed many unwritten family rules on Chen, such as that the washed clothes must satisfy Zhang, that Chen must not talk back when scolded, and that she must not tell others after being beaten. Zhang's control over Chen was also evident from his conduct in the litigation, such as apologizing in his reply and promising not to beat Chen again, but during the trial he threatened, blamed, and belittled Chen, showing his lack of sincerity and remorse. Consequently, the court granted the divorce. Neither party appealed after the first-instance judgment.

Before the first-instance judgment, the court issued a personal safety protection order upon Chen's application, prohibiting Zhang from beating, threatening, stalking, or harassing Chen and their daughter Zhang. The order was valid for six months. Follow-up checks confirmed that Zhang had not violated the order.

Case 4

Li Mou'e v. Luo Mouchao — Divorce Dispute

--Priority Given to the Best Interests of the Child

(1) Basic Facts

The plaintiff Li Mou'e and the defendant Luo Mouchao registered their marriage on January 17, 1994, and gave birth to a daughter, Luo Mouwei, on August 7, 1994, and a son, Luo Mouhai, on June 27, 2002. The couple had a good relationship at first, but from 2003 onward, conflicts arose because Luo frequently drank excessively. From 2011, Luo's heavy drinking worsened, and he often became violent after drinking. Their daughter Luo documented in her diary how Luo beat and scolded Li and the two children when he was drunk. On January 5, 2012, Li filed for divorce for the first time. Because Luo proposed that they register for divorce, Li withdrew the lawsuit. But later Luo reneged, and his drinking and violence became more frequent. On July 30, 2012, Luo, after drinking, threatened to kill the whole family. Li and the children locked themselves in the bedroom to hide, but Luo kicked the door in and beat Li; the children were also beaten while trying to stop him. Li called the police twice that night. By the end of August 2012, to escape the beatings, Li moved out with the children and lived in a rented place, separated from Luo. On September 21, 2012, Li filed for divorce again and requested custody of both children. Luo argued that the relationship was good, denied his drinking and domestic violence, opposed the divorce, and opposed Li having custody.

(2) Judgment

The court found after trial that Luo had long been a heavy drinker and frequently committed domestic violence after drinking. The children Luo Mouwei and Luo Mouhai had witnessed their father beating their mother on several occasions and had also been directly beaten, causing them serious physical and psychological harm and potentially perpetuating the cycle of domestic violence across generations. To prevent the children from continuing to live in a violent environment, custody of both children was awarded to Li, and Luo was ordered to pay child support according to law. Accordingly, the court granted the divorce, awarded custody of the children to Li, and ordered Luo to pay a total of RMB 900 per month in child support. Luo was allowed to visit the children on the first Sunday of each month, provided that he did not drink alcohol within 12 hours before the visit or during the visit; otherwise, the visit would be deemed waived, and Li and the children could refuse the visit. Neither party appealed after the first-instance judgment.

Case 5

Hao Moumou v. Hao Mouhua — Support Dispute

--Personal Safety Protection Order to Stop Elder Abuse by Adult Child

(1) Basic Facts

The applicant Hao Moumou and his late wife Wang had five children. Hao is now unable to work and has no income other than a monthly subsistence allowance of RMB 320. He needs his children to take care of him in daily life. The applicant Hao had been living alternately with his other children except the respondent Hao Mouhua. Because the other children had limited financial means and tight housing, the applicant Hao requested the respondent Hao Mouhua to pay support and provide housing. The respondent Hao Mouhua was dissatisfied with this request and frequently used harsh words to threaten and verbally abuse Hao Moumou, causing him fear and anxiety. Hao Moumou filed a lawsuit, requesting that the respondent pay support and provide housing. After multiple notices from the court, the respondent still failed to appear and instead threatened the plaintiff, leaving the plaintiff in constant fear. During the proceedings, the plaintiff applied to the court for a personal safety protection order, requesting measures to stop the respondent from threatening, verbally abusing, and insulting him.

(2) Judgment

The court found after trial that the applicant's application met legal requirements because the respondent Hao Mouhua frequently used verbal threats and abuse against the applicant, causing the applicant to live in constant fear. The court ruled: the respondent Hao Mouhua is prohibited from using verbal threats, abuse, insults, or any other conduct that may cause the applicant psychological fear, worry, or terror. At the same time, the court admonished the respondent, informing him that if such conduct occurred during the validity period of the order, coercive measures such as detention or fines would be imposed depending on the severity of the violation. Follow-up checks confirmed that the respondent no longer threatened the applicant. With regard to the plaintiff's claim for support, the court ordered the respondent Hao Mouhua to pay the plaintiff RMB 600 per month in support.

Case 6

Zhong Moufang's Application for Post-Divorce Personal Safety Protection

--Post-Divorce Personal Safety Protection Order to Stop "Breakup Violence"

(1) Basic Facts

The applicant Zhong Moufang and the respondent Chen were divorced by court judgment on February 2, 2010, with custody of the children awarded to Zhong. After the judgment took effect, Chen refused to move out of Zhong's house and insisted on eating and sleeping with Zhong, restricting her personal freedom and social interactions. If Zhong showed any resistance, she would be verbally abused and beaten. Chen also repeatedly left threatening notes. After the court compelled him to move out, he still used visiting the children as an excuse to enter Zhong's home multiple times to threaten her, often following and surveilling her movements. This not only caused physical harm to Zhong but also kept her in extreme fear. On May 6, 2010, Zhong applied to the court for a personal safety protection order and submitted evidence including police reports, records of visits to the Women's Federation, threatening notes from the respondent, torn clothes, and photographs.

(2) Judgment

The court found after trial that Zhong continued to be unreasonably harassed by her ex-husband Chen after the divorce, regularly subjected to abuse, beatings, and threats, and still restricted in her personal freedom and social interactions. This was a typical case of control-based violence. To protect the applicant's safety and prevent "breakup violence" from escalating from a civil to a criminal matter, the court ruled: the respondent Chen is prohibited from harassing, stalking, threatening, or beating the applicant Zhong, or having unwanted contact with Zhong and their minor child Chen Moumou; the respondent Chen is prohibited from being within 200 meters of Zhong's residence or workplace; when visiting the child, Chen must obtain the child's consent and must not visit at Zhong's home. The protection order was valid for six months. Follow-up checks confirmed that the applicant was no longer subjected to harm or harassment by the respondent.

Case 7

Deng Rongping — Intentional Injury

--Long-Term Domestic Violence Against Adopted Daughter Results in Prison Sentence

(1) Basic Facts

The victim Fan (female, aged 7 at the time) was adopted by the defendant Deng Rongping shortly after birth. During the adoption period, Deng repeatedly abused Fan by beating her with a wooden stick, burning her with fire, and pinching her with pliers, causing over a hundred lacerations on Fan's head, face, chest, abdomen, and limbs, and the loss of several teeth. On the morning of March 26, 2010, because Fan had wet the bed, Deng beat Fan's legs with a wooden stick, causing a fracture of the left femur, constituting minor injury. After the incident, Deng surrendered to the public security authorities.

(2) Judgment

The court found after trial that the defendant Deng Rongping intentionally injured another person, constituting the crime of intentional injury. As a mother, Deng had long abused her adopted daughter Fan and then beat Fan with a wooden stick over a trivial matter, causing minor injury. The means were cruel, the circumstances egregious, and the consequences serious, warranting punishment according to law. Considering that Deng voluntarily surrendered and truthfully confessed her crime, constituting voluntary surrender, she could be given a lighter punishment according to law. Accordingly, the Guanling Buyi and Miao Autonomous County People's Court sentenced Deng Rongping to two years and two months' imprisonment for intentional injury.

Case 8

Tang Cuilian — Intentional Homicide

--Wife Who Frequently Suffered Domestic Violence Killed Husband and Received Prison Sentence

(1) Basic Facts

The defendant Tang Cuilian and the victim Yang Yuhe (deceased, aged 39) were husband and wife. Yang frequently drank excessively and would beat and scold Tang for no reason after drinking. At around 5:00 p.m. on April 15, 2002, Yang came home drunk, quarreling, and placed several wooden boards at the foot of the wall of a neighbor, Yang Mouhong and his son Yang Mouchun. This led to a dispute and scuffle between Yang Mouchun and Yang Yuhe. Tang Cuilian stepped in to stop them, but Yang Yuhe chased Tang with a wooden stick. Tang grabbed a piece of firewood from a pile and struck Yang Yuhe on the left side of the head, causing him to fall to the ground. Yang Mouhong urged Tang not to hit Yang Yuhe again. Fearing that Yang Yuhe would get up and beat her, Tang continued to strike Yang Yuhe's head with the firewood several times, causing Yang Yuhe to die from a blunt-force head injury causing brain damage. After the incident, the villagers, sympathizing with Tang, advised her not to surrender and helped bury Yang Yuhe's body.

(2) Judgment

The court found after trial that the defendant Tang Cuilian intentionally and unlawfully deprived another person of life, constituting the crime of intentional homicide. The victim Yang Yuhe got into a dispute and scuffle with a neighbor over a trivial matter, and when Tang intervened, Yang chased her with a wooden stick. Tang struck Yang with firewood, causing him to fall, and then, ignoring the neighbor's advice, continued to strike Yang's head, causing his death. The consequences were serious, warranting punishment according to law. However, considering that Yang frequently committed domestic violence after drinking and beat Tang without cause, constituting major fault; that Tang truthfully confessed the facts after the incident with a good attitude; and that local residents requested leniency for Tang, Tang could be given a lighter punishment. Accordingly, the Shidian County People's Court sentenced Tang Cuilian to ten years' imprisonment for intentional homicide.

Case 9

Xiao Zhengxi — Intentional Homicide and Intentional Injury

--Long-Term Domestic Violence and Murder Resulting in Death Penalty

(1) Basic Facts

The defendant Xiao Zhengxi and the victim Xiao Haixia (deceased, aged 26) married in 1998 and had one daughter and one son. In 2005, Xiao Zhengxi suspected Xiao Haixia of having an affair, and the couple's relationship soured. In April 2009, Xiao Haixia filed for divorce, but Xiao Zhengxi did not agree. On May 22, 2010, Xiao Zhengxi forcibly brought Xiao Haixia, who was working away from home, back to the house and injured her. Xiao Haixia's parents reported the matter to the police and took her back to her parents' home in Xingzi County, Jiangxi Province.

On the afternoon of May 25, 2010, Xiao Zhengxi and his cousin Cheng wanted to talk to Xiao Haixia's father Xiao. Xiao refused to meet Xiao Zhengxi. Xiao Zhengxi then bought a cleaver, a fruit knife, a black travel bag, and a flashlight, intending to kill Xiao Haixia. At around 4:00 p.m., ignoring his cousin's劝阻, Xiao Zhengxi took a bus alone to Xiao Haixia's father's house and hid near a pigsty outside the house. At around 11:00 p.m., Xiao Zhengxi entered Xiao Haixia's room and struck her several times on the head, face, and hand with a cleaver, and then stabbed her in the chest with a fruit knife, causing open hemopneumothorax combined with hemorrhagic and traumatic shock, leading to her death. Xiao Zhengxi discarded the fruit knife and fled. Xiao (the father) and his wife Li heard Xiao Haixia's cries for help, chased Xiao Zhengxi, and fought with him. Xiao Zhengxi cut Xiao with the cleaver and cut Li with a utility knife he carried. Xiao Zhengxi was then apprehended by police officers who arrived after receiving the report.

(2) Judgment

The court found after trial that the defendant Xiao Zhengxi intentionally and unlawfully deprived another person of life, constituting the crime of intentional homicide, and intentionally injured another person, constituting the crime of intentional injury. He should be punished for multiple crimes in accordance with the law. Unable to properly handle marital conflicts, Xiao Zhengxi injured Xiao Haixia when she filed for divorce, and later brought weapons to her home and killed her, and stabbed his father-in-law and mother-in-law. The circumstances were extremely egregious and the consequences extremely serious, warranting punishment according to law. Accordingly, the defendant Xiao Zhengxi was sentenced to death and deprived of political rights for life for intentional homicide, and to two years' imprisonment for intentional injury, with the combined punishment being death and deprivation of political rights for life. After review and approval by the Supreme People's Court, the offender Xiao Zhengxi has been executed.

Case 10

Xue Moufeng — Intentional Homicide

--Adopted Daughter Who Was Sexually Abused by Adoptive Father for Years Killed Him and Received Prison Sentence

(1) Basic Facts

The defendant Xue Moufeng was adopted by Xue Moutai (the victim, deceased, aged 54) from childhood. Starting from 1999, when Xue Moufeng was 11 years old, Xue Moutai repeatedly raped her by force. In March 2004, Xue Moufeng became pregnant due to the rape and later had an abortion. In January 2005, Xue Moufeng married another man. On the night of November 11, 2007, Xue Moutai, after drinking, called Xue Moufeng to his room, threatened her with a knife, and demanded sex. Xue Moufeng pretended to agree, and while he was distracted, tied his hands and feet with a rope, then left the room. At around 3:00 a.m. the next day, Xue Moufeng returned to the room, struck Xue Moutai's head with a wrench, causing him to die from brain damage. Xue Moufeng then poured oil on Xue Moutai's body and burned it.

(2) Judgment

The court found after trial that the defendant Xue Moufeng intentionally and unlawfully deprived another person of life, constituting the crime of intentional homicide. The victim Xue Moutai repeatedly sexually abused the defendant over a long period, and on the night of the incident, he attempted to rape her by force, which constituted serious fault by the victim. The defendant had endured years of abuse and killed the victim in the heat of the moment after being threatened with a knife. Her criminal motive was to protect her personal safety and resist the impending sexual assault. Although her act was a crime, the circumstances were mitigating. Considering that the defendant voluntarily surrendered after the incident and truthfully confessed the facts, she could be given a lighter punishment. Accordingly, the court sentenced Xue Moufeng to three years' imprisonment for intentional homicide. Luo was allowed to visit the children on the first Sunday of each month, provided that he did not drink alcohol within 12 hours before the visit or during the visit; otherwise, the visit would be deemed waived, and Li and the children could refuse the visit. Neither party appealed after the first-instance judgment.

Case 5

Hao Moumou v. Hao Mouhua — Support Dispute

--Personal Safety Protection Order to Stop Elder Abuse by Adult Child

(1) Basic Facts

The applicant Hao Moumou and his late wife Wang had five children. Hao is now unable to work and has no income other than a monthly subsistence allowance of RMB 320. He needs his children to take care of him in daily life. The applicant Hao had been living alternately with his other children except the respondent Hao Mouhua. Because the other children had limited financial means and tight housing, the applicant Hao requested the respondent Hao Mouhua to pay support and provide housing. The respondent Hao Mouhua was dissatisfied with this request and frequently used harsh words to threaten and verbally abuse Hao Moumou, causing him fear and anxiety. Hao Moumou filed a lawsuit, requesting that the respondent pay support and provide housing. After multiple notices from the court, the respondent still failed to appear and instead threatened the plaintiff, leaving the plaintiff in constant fear. During the proceedings, the plaintiff applied to the court for a personal safety protection order, requesting measures to stop the respondent from threatening, verbally abusing, and insulting him.

(2) Judgment

The court found after trial that the applicant's application met legal requirements because the respondent Hao Mouhua frequently used verbal threats and abuse against the applicant, causing the applicant to live in constant fear. The court ruled: the respondent Hao Mouhua is prohibited from using verbal threats, abuse, insults, or any other conduct that may cause the applicant psychological fear, worry, or terror. At the same time, the court admonished the respondent, informing him that if such conduct occurred during the validity period of the order, coercive measures such as detention or fines would be imposed depending on the severity of the violation. Follow-up checks confirmed that the respondent no longer threatened the applicant. With regard to the plaintiff's claim for support, the court ordered the respondent Hao Mouhua to pay the plaintiff RMB 600 per month in support.

Case 6

Zhong Moufang's Application for Post-Divorce Personal Safety Protection

--Post-Divorce Personal Safety Protection Order to Stop "Breakup Violence"

(1) Basic Facts

The applicant Zhong Moufang and the respondent Chen were divorced by court judgment on February 2, 2010, with custody of the children awarded to Zhong. After the judgment took effect, Chen refused to move out of Zhong's house and insisted on eating and sleeping with Zhong, restricting her personal freedom and social interactions. If Zhong showed any resistance, she would be verbally abused and beaten. Chen also repeatedly left threatening notes. After the court compelled him to move out, he still used visiting the children as an excuse to enter Zhong's home multiple times to threaten her, often following and surveilling her movements. This not only caused physical harm to Zhong but also kept her in extreme fear. On May 6, 2010, Zhong applied to the court for a personal safety protection order and submitted evidence including police reports, records of visits to the Women's Federation, threatening notes from the respondent, torn clothes, and photographs.

(2) Judgment

The court found after trial that Zhong continued to be unreasonably harassed by her ex-husband Chen after the divorce, regularly subjected to abuse, beatings, and threats, and still restricted in her personal freedom and social interactions. This was a typical case of control-based violence. To protect the applicant's safety and prevent "breakup violence" from escalating from a civil to a criminal matter, the court ruled: the respondent Chen is prohibited from harassing, stalking, threatening, or beating the applicant Zhong, or having unwanted contact with Zhong and their minor child Chen Moumou; the respondent Chen is prohibited from being within 200 meters of Zhong's residence or workplace; when visiting the child, Chen must obtain the child's consent and must not visit at Zhong's home. The protection order was valid for six months. Follow-up checks confirmed that the applicant was no longer subjected to harm or harassment by the respondent.

Case 7

Deng Rongping — Intentional Injury

--Long-Term Domestic Violence Against Adopted Daughter Results in Prison Sentence

(1) Basic Facts

The victim Fan (female, aged 7 at the time) was adopted by the defendant Deng Rongping shortly after birth. During the adoption period, Deng repeatedly abused Fan by beating her with a wooden stick, burning her with fire, and pinching her with pliers, causing over a hundred lacerations on Fan's head, face, chest, abdomen, and limbs, and the loss of several teeth. On the morning of March 26, 2010, because Fan had wet the bed, Deng beat Fan's legs with a wooden stick, causing a fracture of the left femur, constituting minor injury. After the incident, Deng surrendered to the public security authorities.

(2) Judgment

The court found after trial that the defendant Deng Rongping intentionally injured another person, constituting the crime of intentional injury. As a mother, Deng had long abused her adopted daughter Fan and then beat Fan with a wooden stick over a trivial matter, causing minor injury. The means were cruel, the circumstances egregious, and the consequences serious, warranting punishment according to law. Considering that Deng voluntarily surrendered and truthfully confessed her crime, constituting voluntary surrender, she could be given a lighter punishment according to law. Accordingly, the Guanling Buyi and Miao Autonomous County People's Court sentenced Deng Rongping to two years and two months' imprisonment for intentional injury.

Case 8

Tang Cuilian — Intentional Homicide

--Wife Who Frequently Suffered Domestic Violence Killed Husband and Received Prison Sentence

(1) Basic Facts

The defendant Tang Cuilian and the victim Yang Yuhe (deceased, aged 39) were husband and wife. Yang frequently drank excessively and would beat and scold Tang for no reason after drinking. At around 5:00 p.m. on April 15, 2002, Yang came home drunk, quarreling, and placed several wooden boards at the foot of the wall of a neighbor, Yang Mouhong and his son Yang Mouchun. This led to a dispute and scuffle between Yang Mouchun and Yang Yuhe. Tang Cuilian stepped in to stop them, but Yang Yuhe chased Tang with a wooden stick. Tang grabbed a piece of firewood from a pile and struck Yang Yuhe on the left side of the head, causing him to fall to the ground. Yang Mouhong urged Tang not to hit Yang Yuhe again. Fearing that Yang Yuhe would get up and beat her, Tang continued to strike Yang Yuhe's head with the firewood several times, causing Yang Yuhe to die from a blunt-force head injury causing brain damage. After the incident, the villagers, sympathizing with Tang, advised her not to surrender and helped bury Yang Yuhe's body.

(2) Judgment

The court found after trial that the defendant Tang Cuilian intentionally and unlawfully deprived another person of life, constituting the crime of intentional homicide. The victim Yang Yuhe got into a dispute and scuffle with a neighbor over a trivial matter, and when Tang intervened, Yang chased her with a wooden stick. Tang struck Yang with firewood, causing him to fall, and then, ignoring the neighbor's advice, continued to strike Yang's head, causing his death. The consequences were serious, warranting punishment according to law. However, considering that Yang frequently committed domestic violence after drinking and beat Tang without cause, constituting major fault; that Tang truthfully confessed the facts after the incident with a good attitude; and that local residents requested leniency for Tang, Tang could be given a lighter punishment. Accordingly, the Shidian County People's Court sentenced Tang Cuilian to ten years' imprisonment for intentional homicide.

Case 9

Xiao Zhengxi — Intentional Homicide and Intentional Injury

--Long-Term Domestic Violence and Murder Resulting in Death Penalty

(1) Basic Facts

The defendant Xiao Zhengxi and the victim Xiao Haixia (deceased, aged 26) married in 1998 and had one daughter and one son. In 2005, Xiao Zhengxi suspected Xiao Haixia of having an affair, and the couple's relationship soured. In April 2009, Xiao Haixia filed for divorce, but Xiao Zhengxi did not agree. On May 22, 2010, Xiao Zhengxi forcibly brought Xiao Haixia, who was working away from home, back to the house and injured her. Xiao Haixia's parents reported the matter to the police and took her back to her parents' home in Xingzi County, Jiangxi Province.

On the afternoon of May 25, 2010, Xiao Zhengxi and his cousin Cheng wanted to talk to Xiao Haixia's father Xiao. Xiao refused to meet Xiao Zhengxi. Xiao Zhengxi then bought a cleaver, a fruit knife, a black travel bag, and a flashlight, intending to kill Xiao Haixia. At around 4:00 p.m., ignoring his cousin's advice, Xiao Zhengxi took a bus alone to Xiao Haixia's father's house and hid near a pigsty outside the house. At around 11:00 p.m., Xiao Zhengxi entered Xiao Haixia's room and struck her several times on the head, face, and hand with a cleaver, and then stabbed her in the chest with a fruit knife, causing open hemopneumothorax combined with hemorrhagic and traumatic shock, leading to her death. Xiao Zhengxi discarded the fruit knife and fled. Xiao (the father) and his wife Li heard Xiao Haixia's cries for help, chased Xiao Zhengxi, and fought with him. Xiao Zhengxi cut Xiao with the cleaver and cut Li with a utility knife he carried. Xiao Zhengxi was then apprehended by police officers who arrived after receiving the report.

(2) Judgment

The court found after trial that the defendant Xiao Zhengxi intentionally and unlawfully deprived another person of life, constituting the crime of intentional homicide, and intentionally injured another person, constituting the crime of intentional injury. He should be punished for multiple crimes in accordance with the law. Unable to properly handle marital conflicts, Xiao Zhengxi injured Xiao Haixia when she filed for divorce, and later brought weapons to her home and killed her, and stabbed his father-in-law and mother-in-law. The circumstances were extremely egregious and the consequences extremely serious, warranting punishment according to law. Accordingly, the defendant Xiao Zhengxi was sentenced to death and deprived of political rights for life for intentional homicide, and to two years' imprisonment for intentional injury, with the combined punishment being death and deprivation of political rights for life. After review and approval by the Supreme People's Court, the offender Xiao Zhengxi has been executed.

Case 10

Xue Moufeng — Intentional Homicide

--Adopted Daughter Who Was Sexually Abused by Adoptive Father for Years Killed Him and Received Prison Sentence

(1) Basic Facts

The defendant Xue Moufeng was adopted by Xue Moutai (the victim, deceased, aged 54) from childhood. Starting from 1999, when Xue Moufeng was 11 years old, Xue Moutai repeatedly raped her by force. In March 2004, Xue Moufeng became pregnant due to the rape and later had an abortion. In January 2005, Xue Moufeng married another man. On the night of November 11, 2007, Xue Moutai, after drinking, called Xue Moufeng to his room, threatened her with a knife, and demanded sex. Xue Moufeng pretended to agree, and while he was distracted, tied his hands and feet with a rope, then left the room. At around 3:00 a.m. the next day, Xue Moufeng returned to the room, struck Xue Moutai's head with a wrench, causing him to die from brain damage. Xue Moufeng then poured oil on Xue Moutai's body and burned it.

(2) Judgment

The court found after trial that the defendant, Xue A, had intentionally and unlawfully deprived another person of life, constituting the crime of intentional homicide. Xue A struck the victim, Xue B, on the head with a weapon, causing his death. The consequences were serious, and she should be punished according to law. In view of the fact that Xue B, taking advantage of his status as adoptive father, had long-term raped Xue A from the time she was a young girl, causing her to become pregnant and undergo an induced abortion, which caused enormous physical and psychological harm to Xue A; and even after Xue A married another person, Xue B still attempted to forcibly rape her with a knife, showing that he was at substantial fault; the Linzhang County People's Procuratorate considered that, because Xue A had been long-term raped by Xue B since childhood, her killing of Xue B in resistance constituted intentional homicide under relatively minor circumstances, and recommended that a suspended sentence be applied to Xue A; the local village committee and hundreds of residents jointly requested a lenient punishment for Xue A on the grounds that her act of killing was truly intolerable and that she had two young children and a mentally disabled adoptive mother at home who needed care; the Linzhang County Women's Federation recommended that, to save Xue A's family and reduce social disharmony, the most lenient punishment possible be imposed; after the incident, Xue A had a good attitude in admitting guilt and showed remorse. In summary, the defendant Xue A may be given a lenient punishment. Accordingly, the Linzhang County People's Court sentenced the defendant Xue A to three years' imprisonment, suspended for five years, for the crime of intentional homicide, according to law.
